deferred_source_units.source_text: From heaven Thou didst cause judgment to be heard; the earth feared and grew quiet,
deferred_source_units.reason: The psalm combines judgment heard from heaven with the earth fearing and growing quiet. Zechariah calls all flesh to reverence because the Lord rose from His holy clouds, but does not state the anticipated silence or heard judgment. The remaining broad divine-appearance response does not establish the proposed particular parallel.

deferred_source_units.source_text: I am poor and in toils from my youth; but after being raised up, I was humbled and left helpless.
deferred_source_units.reason: The source explicitly places humiliation and helplessness after being raised up. The actual Job passage speaks of being placed amid pains and cast away from salvation; it does not describe the anticipated lifting by wind or that raised-then-humbled sequence. That expected alternative wording is not supplied, and shared affliction alone is insufficient.

deferred_source_units.source_text: I opened my mouth and drew breath, for I longed for Thy commandments.
deferred_source_units.reason: The source opens the mouth and draws breath in longing for commandments. Job describes hearers awaiting his speech like thirsty earth awaiting rain; the expected opening of their mouths is absent. Desire for words alone does not establish the proposed particular mouth-and-breath correspondence.

target_units.text: I have cried to Thee, and Thou dost not hear me; they stood and observed me.
Thou camest upon me without mercy; with a mighty hand Thou didst scourge me.
Thou didst place me amid pains and cast me away from salvation.
For I know that death will wear me away; for earth is the house of every mortal.

target_units.text: When they heard me, they paid attention and kept silent at my counsel.
They added nothing to my word, and became overjoyed whenever I spoke to them.
Like thirsty earth awaiting rain, so they awaited my speech.
